speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history; I see you have a significant medical background. To understand the cause of your gait and limb ataxia, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the "drunk" appearance and right-sided clumsiness are concerning. Does the ataxia worsen significantly when you look to your left, or do you experience any double vision or difficulty swallowing? Also, have you noticed any involuntary eye movements?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast; REQUEST TEST: Antibody panel (Anti-MOG, Anti-GFAP).

DIAGNOSIS READY: ADEM (Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis) likely triggered by natalizumab therapy, given the atypical presentation in a Crohn's patient despite prior MS diagnosis.
